title: Optimized protocol for whole-mount RNA fluorescent in situ hybridization using oxidation-mediated autofluorescence reduction on mouse embryos
author: Morabito, Malkmus, et al.
materials: EDTA disodium salt 2-hydrate for molecular biology

steps.title: Prepare 4 % PFA fixative
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 g paraformaldehyde powder in 25 mL PBS (pH 7.4) while heating to 50–60 °C in a chemical hood until fully dissolved; wear gloves and handle as a toxic carcinogen, dispose waste in a dedicated formaldehyde container.

steps.title: Detergent permeabilization of limb buds
steps.instruction: Transfer 4–6 mouse limb buds into 1 mL PBST in a clean 2 mL microcentrifuge tube, remove PBST, add 1 mL Detergent Solution (4 % SDS for limb buds; can be reduced to 1 % for smaller/fragile samples) and incubate 2 h at 37 °C on a shaker at 300 rpm. Store the Detergent Solution in the dark at 24 °C for up to 1 month.

steps.title: Wash after detergent treatment
steps.instruction: Remove the Detergent Solution and wash the limb buds twice with 1 mL PBST for 5 min at room temperature (24 °C).

steps.title: Pre‑equilibrate in probe hybridization buffer
steps.instruction: Equilibrate the limb buds in 100 µL Probe Hybridization Buffer (Molecular Instruments) for 10 min at 24 °C on a shaker at 300 rpm.

steps.title: Pre‑hybridization incubation
steps.instruction: Replace with 200 µL pre‑warmed (37 °C) Probe Hybridization Buffer and incubate ≥1 h (or longer) at 37 °C, 300 rpm. Limb buds may be stored in this buffer at –20 °C for several months.

steps.title: Prepare HCR probe mixes
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL of each probe set (1 µM stock) to 100 µL pre‑warmed (37 °C) Probe Hybridization Buffer to make the probe mix.

steps.title: Hybridize probes
steps.instruction: Remove the pre‑hybridization solution, add 100 µL of the prepared probe mix per tube, and incubate 12–16 h at 37 °C on a shaker at 300 rpm.

steps.title: Probe wash series
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL pre‑warmed Probe Wash Buffer, then perform four washes of 20 min each at 37 °C with shaking at 300 rpm.

steps.title: Wash with 5× SSCT
steps.instruction: Remove Probe Wash Buffer and wash three times with 1 mL 5× SSCT (pH 7.4) for 20 min per wash at room temperature (24 °C). Store 5× SSCT at 24 °C.

steps.title: Pre‑equilibrate amplification buffer
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL pre‑equilibrated Amplification Buffer (kept at 24 °C) and incubate 5 min at 24 °C.

steps.title: Pre‑amplification and hairpin preparation
steps.instruction: Replace with fresh 200 µL pre‑equilibrated Amplification Buffer and incubate ≥1 h at 24 °C. Meanwhile, heat hairpins H1 and H2 separately for 90 s at 95 °C, cool 30 min at 24 °C in the dark, then mix 2 µL of each (3 µM stock) per fluorophore in 100 µL Amplification Buffer. Protect all tubes from light.

steps.title: Amplification with hairpins
steps.instruction: Replace the buffer with 100 µL hairpin mix per tube and incubate 12–16 h on a shaker (300 rpm) at 24 °C, keeping tubes protected from light.

steps.title: Post‑amplification washes
steps.instruction: Wash the limb buds three times for 5 min with 1 mL 5× SSCT at 24 °C on a rocking platform (20 oscillations/min); protect from light. Store used hairpin mixes in the dark at 4 °C (short‑term) or –20 °C (long‑term).

steps.title: DAPI staining
steps.instruction: Transfer samples to a clean tube, protect from light, and wash six times for 30 min each in 1 mL 5× SSCT containing DAPI (1 : 1000 dilution from a 1 mg/mL stock stored at –20 °C, dark). If DAPI is not required, wash six times with 5× SSCT only.

steps.title: Final SSCT washes before clearing
steps.instruction: Transfer limb buds to a new tube (protected from light) and wash three times for 5 min with 1 mL 5× SSCT (no DAPI). Samples are now ready for optical clearing; they may be stored in dark 5× SSCT for several days.

steps.title: Fructose‑Glycerol optical clearing
steps.instruction: Place limb buds in a new multi‑well plate (protected from light), add freshly prepared Fructose‑Glycerol‑Clearing solution (pH 7.4), and clear for 24 h at 24 °C on a rocking platform (20 oscillations/min). Extend to 48–72 h if needed, exchanging the solution every 24 h with freshly prepared solution.

steps.title: Permeabilize for immunofluorescence
steps.instruction: Wash photochemically bleached samples three times for 10 min each in 1 mL 0.4 % Triton X‑100 in PBS at 24 °C on a rocking platform (20 oscillations/min). Remove Triton solution.

steps.title: Block before antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL Blocking solution (without donkey serum, stored at 4 °C; fresh donkey serum added just before use) and incubate ≥45 min at 24 °C. Remove Blocking solution.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Add primary antibody diluted in Blocking solution (typical 1 : 50–1 : 200), centrifuge at 1500 g for 10 min to remove precipitates, transfer supernatant, and incubate 16–20 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash after primary antibody
steps.instruction: Wash six times with 1 mL 0.1 % Triton X‑100 in PBS (pH 7.4) for 30 min each at 24 °C on a rocking platform (20 oscillations/min).

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Add secondary antibody in 0.4 % Triton X‑100 in PBS, 1 % BSA, 10 % serum, containing DAPI (1 : 1000), incubate 16–20 h at 4 °C in the dark (typical dilution 1 : 200–1 : 2000).

steps.title: Final washes before clearing
steps.instruction: Wash with 1 mL 0.1 % Triton X‑100 in PBS for 3 h at 24 °C, changing solution minimally six times (≈30 min intervals). Samples are now ready for optical clearing (continue from the clearing step above).

description: Tissue autofluorescence emanating from various sources poses a complex challenge for high-sensitivity detection of fluorescently labelled RNA probes and antibody staining.1 Although these problems can -in some cases- be ameliorated by post-processing of raw images.2 It is preferable to eliminate tissue autofluorescence at the source and prior to fluorescent labelling. Therefore, various pre-treatments such as irradiation-by-light or chemicals are used to eliminate autofluorescence on tissue sections.3,4,5,6,7 At the same time, this has remained challenging for fluorescence detection on whole mounts such as embryos, tissues, and organs. Here, we describe the adaptation of a photochemical pre-treatment8 suited for fluorescent whole-mount analysis that consistently reduces and most often eliminates tissue and blood vessel autofluorescence. The OMAR treatment improves the signal-to-noise ratio for whole-mount Hybridization Chain Reaction (HCR) RNA fluorescent in situ hybridization (RNA-FISH). This study also shows that OMAR can be used for whole-mount immunofluorescence analysis. Briefly, OMAR requires a high-intensity cold white light source. For example, high-power LED spotlights on flexible goosenecks (Figure 1A) or two LED daylight panels (20000 lumen) can be used (Figure 1B). As autofluorescence varies significantly between tissues, the efficacy of the available LED light source(s) in eliminating autofluorescence must be established in a test series. Use the fixed tissues or organs of interest to carry out steps 1–10 of the step-by-step protocol, followed by mounting and imaging the samples. Successful oxidation reaction manifests itself by the appearance of an increasing number and size of bubbles in the solution and around the sample during the two photochemical pre-treatments (Figure 1C).
